scope: finite exact microscopes for F3 rows 5 through 9
claim_boundary: These are bounded interaction laws. They do not establish G6 capability prediction, universal monotone synergy, or empirical transfer.

rows.scope: finite learner state crossed with a finite teaching transcript alphabet
assumptions: the learner begins in one of P prior-equivalence classes
the complete teaching transcript has at most K distinguishable values
the learner receives no additional side information
exact teaching requires preserving each obligation-distinct prior/transcript cell
rows.theorem: After teaching, the learner can occupy at most P*K distinguishable prior/transcript cells. More than P*K obligation-distinct lesson outcomes cannot be taught exactly under the declared channel; the bound is tight by injective encoding when the required cells fit.
rows.strongest_parent: finite communication complexity plus pedagogical state update
rows.negative_twin: make the target independent of the teaching transcript; K drops out and communication has no pedagogical value
rows.nearest_counterexample: interactive side channels or an uncharged shared codebook can enlarge the effective transcript alphabet
rows.falsifier: an exact learner distinguishing more than P*K required cells without extra information

rows.scope: deterministic one-generation ratchet with itemwise transmission and novel discovery
assumptions: current repertoire has R distinct useful items
teaching can transmit at most K existing items exactly
the learner independently adds B genuinely novel useful items
transmitted and newly discovered items are retained without duplication
rows.theorem: The maximum next-generation repertoire is min(R,K)+B. Strict cumulative growth occurs iff B > max(0,R-K). Thus teaching capacity determines how much rediscovery must merely replace transmission loss before culture can accumulate.
rows.strongest_parent: cultural transmission / retention recurrence with finite channel capacity
rows.negative_twin: set B=0; repertoire cannot grow and falls to min(R,K) when teaching is lossy
rows.nearest_counterexample: compression or compositional teaching can transmit more than K itemwise units and lies outside this itemwise scope
rows.falsifier: a repertoire larger than min(R,K)+B under the stated itemwise accounting

rows.scope: finite optional computations with equal unit cost and additive expected net gains
assumptions: each optional computation has a registered expected value of computation (EVC)
all optional computations consume one identical budget slot
net gains add and there are no interaction terms
at most k computations may be funded
rows.theorem: An optimal allocation funds the k largest positive EVCs (or all positive EVCs if fewer than k). Scarcity is load-bearing: when k covers every positive-EVC operation, ranking information no longer changes the selected set.
rows.strongest_parent: rational metareasoning under equal-cost additive actions
rows.negative_twin: make all EVCs equal and positive; metacognitive ranking provides no allocation advantage
rows.nearest_counterexample: unequal costs or nonadditive computation interactions turn the problem into a different allocation problem; the top-k theorem need not hold
rows.falsifier: an equal-cost additive instance where a non-top-k-positive set has larger total EVC

rows.scope: finite latent worlds represented by model classes with exact intervention action values
assumptions: each latent world has a finite action-value vector under intervention
the planner observes only a registered model-class label
within a model class the planner must choose one action
planning success means choosing an action optimal in every latent world compatible with the observed class
rows.theorem: A model representation is exactly planning-sufficient iff, for every represented class, the intersection of the argmax action sets of all compatible worlds is nonempty. Observational aliasing is harmless only when aliased worlds retain a common optimal intervention.
rows.negative_twin: make all aliased worlds share the same optimal intervention; observationally coarse state becomes planning-sufficient
rows.nearest_counterexample: if the planner can actively disambiguate the latent world before acting, a currently insufficient class may become sufficient after information acquisition
rows.falsifier: a class with empty common-optimal-action intersection that nevertheless supports one exact class-conditioned action

rows.scope: ordered finite routed proposals, bounded verification prefix, deterministic accept predicate
assumptions: the router produces an ordered proposal list
the verifier may inspect at most q routed proposals
safe adoption requires every accepted inspected proposal to be correct
success additionally requires at least one accepted correct inspected proposal
rows.theorem: Guaranteed safe success occurs iff the verifier is sound on the inspected prefix and that prefix contains at least one accepted correct proposal. Routing proposals beyond q cannot improve the guarantee unless routing changes which proposals enter the verified prefix.
rows.strongest_parent: solver routing plus bounded verification / selective prediction
rows.negative_twin: set q=0; no routed proposal can be safely adopted regardless of router breadth
rows.nearest_counterexample: a verifier that can batch-certify uninspected proposals changes the effective verification budget and lies outside the prefix model
rows.falsifier: safe guaranteed adoption without a correct accepted proposal in the verified prefix, or safe adoption despite an accepted incorrect inspected proposal
